current.text: The Spurs' projected starters are Fox, Castle, Vassell, Harris and Wembanyama.
The Spurs stagger Fox, Castle and Harper so that at least two of them are always on the court. More three-guard lineups are expected this season.

Most experts expect him to come off the bench to start the year and to have to earn a starting spot. One expert notes the Spurs' point guard depth is poor and that they may start Harper, Castle and Fox together.

Experts disagree on his minutes. One expects him to push toward 30 minutes even off the bench. Others say a crowded backcourt limits him, because the Spurs will not bench Fox or Castle and a healthier Fox takes minutes.
Experts expect his strong late-season shooting from last season not to last.
If his late-season shooting holds, one expert sees him as a top five player in the league.
Experts call him over drafted at an ADP of about 70 to 84. They see his fair value closer to rank 100 and say he leaves no value inside the top 80.
Drafters take him mainly for assists.
Experts call him a poor points-league pick. That is no direct guide for our category league.
The Spurs are projected as a top team in the West. One host predicts 63 wins.
The Spurs have a very deep rotation that coach Mitch Johnson must balance.

durable.text: The Spurs see him as a future superstar and part of their long-term backcourt with Castle.
He is a much better defender than people think.
No category in his projected line is weak enough to flag, so he fits any build without filling one category in a big way.

note: Yahoo values him at 11 USD but drafters pay about 5.4 USD. ESPN has him at 2 USD and rank 101, which matches the experts' view that he is worth about rank 100, not top 80. In a 144-player draft he is a balanced, all-build bench guard worth about 4 to 6 USD. His projections assume a jump from 22.6 to about 29 minutes. Early in the season, check whether he starts or gets close to 30 minutes next to Fox and Castle, and whether his 50% FG holds.
